articles.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
articles.summary: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday. José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months.
body: The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too.

“The clásico is just another game in the championship but to say it’s a game like any other would be to lie, totally unreal,” Mourinho said on Wednesday, and he knows. As for Barcelona’s latest star, he’s looking forward to seeing Mourinho again. “I love the needle,” Lamine Yamal says. “The Mourinho-Guardiola era, I loved all that. That’s football. Sport is serious but I want a show and we have more fun.”

articles.title: The sexual assault scandal rocked gymnastics – but has pace of change in the sport been too slow?
articles.summary: Former USA team doctor Larry Nassar’s 2018 conviction sparked a global reckoning in gymnastics, yet gymnasts say they are still being let down. It has been 10 years since the Indianapolis Star published allegations of sexual abuse by Larry Nassar, the former team doctor for USA Gymnastics, setting…
body: The exposure of his crimes sparked a wider investigation into how gymnastics had allowed predators to abuse young athletes around the world. While Nassar was the worst recorded case, it emerged many other countries had questions to answer about the failure to protect victims from not only sexual but physical and emotional abuse. But a decade later, on a large houseboat moored in Rotterdam three tram stops away from the Ahoy Arena, where the World Gymnastics Championships are taking place this week, survivors and advocates raised fears about the slow pace of change.

The impact of the Nassar case was seismic, not least because of the decision of Judge Rosemarie Aquilina, on agreeing to Nassar’s plea deal, to allow his victims to have their say in her courtroom. People tuned into Aquilina’s courtroom from all over the world to watch as 169 people took to the stand across seven days, delivering blistering, emotionally charged and brave testimonies of Nassar’s abuse and the impact of that abuse. Aquilina sentenced him to up to 175 years in jail with other convictions, federal and state, making a total of 300 years to life.

articles.title: Fastest pitch in World Series history as Brewers win opener
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 3-2 in the opening game of the best-of-seven World Series as both sides aim for their first title.
body: Milwaukee Brewers starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski threw the fastest recorded pitch in World Series history as his side began the best-of-seven season finale with a win.
The right-hander played a starring role in the 3-2 win at home to the Tampa Bay Rays, in the first match of the 122nd World Series.
It is only the second time in more than a century that neither side contesting the World Series has won the title before.
A sell-out crowd watched the Brewers in only their second appearance in the finale of the Major League Baseball season, and their first since losing to the St Louis Cardinals in 1982.

articles.title: Daniel Stewart, former Port Adelaide AFL player, dies aged 37
articles.summary: Key forward played 36 games and kicked 31 goals between 2010 and 2013. Power will wear black armbands at first home game of 2027 season. Former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart has died suddenly at the age of 37.
body: The Power confirmed Stewart’s death on Saturday as the club said it was “deeply saddened” by the news that had come as a “shock”.
Stewart played 36 AFL matches and kicked 31 goals for the Power between 2010 and 2013 after being selected with pick No 35 in the 2009 rookie draft.
The 200cm key forward was recruited from North Adelaide in the Sanfl, after coming through the Eastern Ranges and Queensland club Labrador.
Stewart was promoted to the Power’s senior list at the end of the 2009 season and the next year made his debut in round four against Geelong.

articles.title: Brewers survive chaotic ninth-inning replay drama to beat Rays in World Series opener
articles.summary: Brewers claim 3-2 victory in Game 1 of World Series. Yelich triples home a run and scores in first inning. Misiorowski and Megill hold off late Rays fightback. Trevor Megill struck out Jonny DeLuca with runners on second and third to escape a ninth-inning jam as the Milwaukee Brewers held on for a…
body: DeLuca’s strikeout came after Tampa Bay’s Liam Hicks had grounded into an apparent game-ending double play that was overturned after a video review. Replays showed that Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt’s right foot was slightly off the bag when he reached to catch a high throw from second baseman Brice Turang.

“You have a big range of emotions,” Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich said. “It’s a big credit to Trev for locking back in right there and making some huge pitches after you have that emotional dump and then have to get back on it.”
Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run and four hits over five innings to earn the victory.

articles.title: Volkanovski nears featherweight immortality as record beckons
articles.summary: Alexander Volkanovski will stake his claim to be the greatest featherweight of all time if he beats Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi on Saturday.
body: Alexander Volkanovski is already widely regarded as one of the best featherweights of all time, but is he about to become the greatest?
Now in his second championship run, the 38-year-old will earn a record ninth win in UFC featherweight title fights if he triumphs against the Russian.
Victory would allow Volkanovski to surpass Brazilian icon Jose Aldo, whom many regard as the best featherweight of all time.
Fans and pundits have hotly debated the topic of the greatest featherweight, with American Max Holloway also considered among the best, but the modest Volkanovski refuses to engage with it.

articles.title: Canada inflict back-to-back losses on England
articles.summary: England suffer back-to-back defeats for the first time in a decade as Canada win 31-22 in Ottawa, including a hat-trick for captain Sophie de Goede.
body: Head coach John Mitchell said England need a "new stimulus" after losing 31-22 to Canada in the WXV Series in Ottawa to suffer back-to-back defeats for the first time in a decade.
It completes a 2-0 series win for Canada after the two sides also shared a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September.

After losing multiple matches in a calendar year for the first time since 2016, world champions England head into their meeting with the USA in New Jersey next Friday (21:15 GMT) hoping to avoid three consecutive losses for the first time since 2013.

England made a promising start, Maddie Feaunati crashing over from close range inside 10 minutes, but Canada hit back twice in quick succession through Julia Omokhuale and De Goede to lead 12-7 at the break.

articles.title: Red Bull identifies two "key focus" areas after Max Verstappen's promising start in Austin
articles.summary: Max Verstappen finished Friday's practice sessions for the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix in second and third place. In both sessions, the four-time world champion was less than two tenths behind Charles Leclerc, who set the benchmark on both occasions.
body: Red Bull is not immediately standing out from the rest of the field as it did in Malaysia, for example, but Verstappen is nevertheless largely satisfied with the early signs from the RB22 in Texas.
"It's been a positive start to the weekend. This track is never easy when it comes to finding the right compromise between the low and high-speed corners", the Dutchman said after FP2.

"The bumps make it even more difficult, so you’re trying to find a good balance in the car and get into a rhythm. That’s what we’ve been working on between FP1 and FP2. There’s still a bit more work to do to fine-tune that balance, but it wasn’t a bad day at all."

In practical terms, this means teams have to find a compromise in two different ways this weekend. Given the varied layout of the Circuit of the Americas, the first concerns the balance between high-speed and low-speed corners. Based on the GPS data, Red Bull appears competitive in the high-speed sections, making technical director Pierre Wache very clear about what needs to improve.

articles.title: Smith v Puello world title fight predictions
articles.summary: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Saturday's light-welterweight title fight between WBC champion Dalton Smith and Alberto Puello.
body: Dalton Smith will make the first defence of his WBC light-welterweight title on home soil when he faces former champion Alberto Puello in Sheffield on Saturday.
Unbeaten Smith, 29, returns to the ring for the first time since becoming world champion with a stunning knockout of Subriel Matias in New York in January.
Dominican Republic fighter Puello, 32, is aiming to become a three-time world champion, having lost his WBC belt to Matias on points last year.
Smith will have the backing of his home crowd at the Utilita Arena. Can he keep his dream of fighting at Sheffield Wednesday's Hillsborough stadium alive with another win?

articles.title: Xabi Alonso welcomes “special” Chelsea–Tottenham Derby and urges Blues to keep cool
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso has said he is looking forward to the 'special' experience of a London Derby between Chelsea and Tottenham. Chelsea welcome their fierce rivals to Stamford Bridge in the Premier League this evening.
body: Chelsea have won their last six meetings with Spurs in all competitions, and have lost just one league game against their London neighbours at Stamford Bridge in 34 meetings.
Asked how he feels ahead of the game, Alonso expressed his excitement but warned Chelsea must keep their cool.
"Every derby is special, you feel the energy and excitement from the stands. We need to use that energy on the pitch because we need to connect well," he said at his pre-match press conference.
"We need to have good emotional control as well because there is a lot of passion and commitment from both sides. Playing football with heart is what we want."

articles.title: 'Like a mini World Cup' - Jacks sees positives in England's tri-series troubles
articles.summary: Will Jacks intends to treat England's next two tri-series matches as a mini World Cup after defeats by Pakistan and Sri Lanka in their opening two matches boxed them into must-win territory.
body: England had looked set to bounce back from an 87-run hammering by Pakistan as Harry Brook's record-breaking 202 saw Sri Lanka set a massive 430 to win their match on Thursday, only for them to pull off a remarkable run chase on the penultimate ball.

The two-wicket defeat means England arrive in Lahore knowing they must beat both Pakistan on Sunday and then Sri Lanka on Thursday to give themselves a chance of of reaching the final on Saturday, October 31.

Jacks pointed out that England were faced with a similar predicament en route to winning the 2019 World Cup and, looking ahead to 2027 edition in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, he views this next week as important preparation.
"It's my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup-style pressure." Jacks told the Press Association on Friday. "You can't replicate that in training or a bilateral series.

articles.title: Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg defends verbal jousting with Luka Doncic: ‘He's not Michael Jordan'
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 18 points and 13 rebounds in his home debut Friday, but it wasn't enough to keep the Warriors from collapsing late in a painful loss to Memphis.
body: This time Yaxel Lendeborg squared off against Cameron Boozer, not Luka Doncic. That made for a different type of duel, without any referendum on whether an NBA rookie should dare trade trash talk with one of the league's top players.
Doncic's name still came up Friday night at Chase Center, and once again Lendeborg showed his penchant for biting honesty.

"I'm always gonna be myself, man," Lendeborg said after he and the Golden State Warriors collapsed late and fell 111-108 to Memphis. "I don't care what anybody has to say about it. The guys on the couch talking bad about me, I couldn't care less.
"I'm 24 and in the NBA, with the best job in the world. I just moved my mom out to California. I'm living a dream."

articles.title: Newey responds to Horner's 'abandon ship' criticism
articles.summary: Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book.
body: Horner as team principal and Newey as technical chief worked together with huge success across 19 years at Red Bull, enjoying two periods of sustained title-winning form with first Sebastian Vettel in 2010-2013 and then Max Verstappen in 2021-2024.
But between those periods Red Bull took a back seat to Mercedes' dominance of the sport following the arrival of turbo-hybrid engines in 2014.

Red Bull initially continued to be powered by Renault, as in their four title-winning years under the previous rules era, but the French manufacturer struggled with the new regulations, which compromised the performance of the team's Newey-designed car.

Writing in his newly-released autobiography, Drive, Horner recounted a period mid-way through 2014 when he became disappointed in Newey after the legendary designer had received an offer to join Ferrari and was mulling whether to leave.

articles.summary: Issa Diop escaped what Oliver Glasner called "a clear red card" during Ipswich's 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest - but the incident split opinion, so was it the right call or not?
body: With less than five minutes of the second half played when Diop slid in on Forest's James McAtee, a sending off could have transformed the outcome of the game.

Glasner was adamant Diop had denied a clear goal-scoring opportunity. But Diop himself told Sky Sports he was "quite confident" he would stay on the field as the officials and VAR came to their decision.
On co-commentary, Lee Hendrie reckoned Diop was "really lucky" and criticised the reasoning from the referee. Post-match, Ashley Young defended the decision.
Here we break down the key moment - and ask you to have your say.
